 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 4 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 831 of 2015
 Sonam
 Versus

 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellant
 Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the respo
 Order

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is taken note of that the notice has been served on respondent No.1.
The respondent Nos.1 and 2 are real brothers and they had earlier filed MA No.948/2015 which was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 18.03.2019.
As such, this appeal is being heard in their absence, as despite service none has appeared on their behalf and their appeal has already been dismissed.

2. The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 02.01.2015 passed in claim case No.47/11 whereby challenging the quantum of compensation.
3. The brief facts of the case are that the appellant was coming towards Ganeshdas Road on 09.10.2010 at around 06:30 in the morning.

The respondent No.1 came riding Hero Honda Passion motorcycle which was new having no registration number, it dashed into the appellant, who was 2 MA-831-2015 riding her bicycle because of which the appellant received grievous injuries on her head and other parts of the body.
Her head suffered comminuted fracture and injuries on her right eye.
Her cheek bone of right side was also got fractured.
Soft tissues of her head got damaged resulting in blood clots.
All injuries in the head resulted in loss of eye sight in her right eye completely and disfiguration of the face.
She also lost some of her ability to comprehend because of injuries on her head.
The appellant was 17 years of age on the date of accident.
She was treated at Vishesh Hospital, Indore from 09.10.2010 to 15.10.2010 thereafter she was treated at different eye hospitals for recovering her eye sight in right eye but to no avail.

4. The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for the injuries sustained by her in the aforesaid accident as well as for permanent disability in loss of eye sight in her left eye.

The claims tribunal after recording evidence concluded that it was the mistake of the rider of the insured vehicle/Hero Honda Motorcycle which caused permanent disability and other injuries to the appellant.
Resultantly, a total compensation to the tune of Rs.3,48,700/- was awarded to her.

1 5.

The claims tribunal while considering the quantification of compensation has assessed income at Rs.3000/- per month which the learned counsel disputes by asserting that the appellant was a student at the time of her accident.
Her future was bright and the claims tribunal should have considered her income at least as per the minimum wages prescribed for the skilled labourer.
He submits that at the relevant time the wages for skilled labourer were Rs.4425/- per month.

He further submits that in other heads 3 MA-831-2015 meager amount of compensation has been awarded and less amount has been awarded for loss of marriage prospects although she has suffered disfiguration of her face and loss of eye sight in her right eye.
Even no addition has been made under the head of future prospects.
Thus, he prays for enhancement of compensation for loss of earning capacity and other heads also.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company supports the findings of the award and submits that claims tribunal has correctly assessed the extent of loss of earning capacity at 30% and as there was no material to establish the income of the appellant, considering that she was only a student at the time of accident, the claims tribunal has correctly taken her income at Rs.3000/- per month on notional basis and supports the findings of the impugned award.

He further points out that the claims tribunal has considered the breach of terms of insurance policy,
however, directed for pay and recover.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

From perusal of the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 26 of the impugned award, it is apparent that the claims tribunal while considering the documents of the appellant has taken her age between 17-19 years and for the reason of absence of any material to establish her income, her income was assessed at Rs.3000/- per month notionally.

Considering the fact that the appellant was a student and a minor girl on the date of her accident, her income is taken as Rs.4425/- per month based on the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority prescribing minimum wages at 4 MA-831-2015 that rate for a skilled labourer.

9. Considering the fact that the appellant was put in the age bracket of 17- 19 on the date of the accident by the claims tribunal itself, in view of the column No.4 of the table provided in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104, multiplier of 18 is applied on the said income and in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others,
2017 (16) SCC 680, 40% addition is made in her income.

sentences.text: 10. Considering the fact that the appellant has suffered disfiguration of her face, loss of eye sight in her right eye and loss of comprehension due to clot in brain, the amount awarded for these injuries at Rs.50,000/- is hereby modified to Rs.1 Lac.
The amount for transportation is hereby modified from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
The amount of medical expenses is maintained as it is.

As such,
now the total compensation comes to Rs.6,37,336/- and after deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.3,48,700/-, the appellant is entitled for payment of Rs.2,88,636/- which shall be paid to the appellant with interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
The other terms of the award shall remain intact.

2 11.
Learned counsel for the appellant points out that initially he had paid court fees @10% on the valuation of the appeal, however, the same was subsequently amended retrospectively to 2.50%.
thus, he submits that he has paid excess court fees and prays for refund of the same.
12. Office is directed to verify this fact and if there is any excess court 5 MA-831-2015 fees, the same be refunded.
13. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
